I am an old man now, 58 years, and I have been growing cashew here in Mtwara all my life like my father before me. For this small plot of nuts, I will not buy the chemical fertilizer — it is expensive and for cashew here we rarely use it, the trees manage with our sandy soil. I will spray pesticide because without sulfur dusting the powdery mildew will destroy my flowers and I will have no harvest to sell. My sons help me with the slashing and harvesting, but at picking time I must hire some young men from the village because the nuts fall over many weeks and I cannot gather them alone.
